summary.text: Cordis composes tools, providers, sessions and even the agent loop as plugins.

maturity.text: Developer preview: 0.1.6-alpha.2 at this snapshot. The project explicitly warns of breaking changes and unaudited safety.

advantages.text: The replaceable loop and typed service seams make agent composition directly inspectable.
Append-only sessions provide a clear relationship between logged events and model context.

tradeoffs.text: Profiles, bundles, presets and plugin lifecycles add concepts for a new contributor to learn.
External host plugins run in-process with host-user authority, outside the workspace sandbox.

taskFit.text: Research and custom harnesses that replace tools, providers, persistence or the loop itself.
Inspecting long-running work across web, headless and programmatic interfaces.

nodes.label: Profile + bundles
nodes.subtitle: Choose the capability set

responsibility.text: Composes ordered patches for web, headless, SDK or ACP environments.

nodes.extension: Profiles can layer additional bundles and patches.
nodes.failureMode: Changing a profile can alter which services and tools are available.

nodes.label: Web / SDK / ACP
nodes.subtitle: User and protocol surfaces

responsibility.text: Presents runtime events through browser, headless and programmatic clients.

nodes.failureMode: A UI feature is not automatically present in every runtime profile.

nodes.label: Cordis context
nodes.subtitle: Services + typed events

responsibility.text: Hosts a plugin tree with typed services, events and reversible registrations.

nodes.extension: Even central services can be supplied by plugins.
nodes.failureMode: Service dependencies and plugin unloading must be handled consistently.

nodes.label: Agent-loop plugin
nodes.subtitle: Prompt → sample → tools

responsibility.text: Claims input, prepares the prompt, runs interception events and continues sampling while more work remains.

nodes.extension: The loop itself can be replaced.
nodes.failureMode: Interceptors can change or reject a step; event ordering matters.

nodes.label: Guarded tool pipeline
nodes.subtitle: Pre → execute → post

responsibility.text: Routes calls through typed interception around execution. Parallel-safe tools share a bounded pool; exclusive calls form barriers.

nodes.extension: Tools and before/after handlers are plugins.
nodes.failureMode: Incorrect concurrency declarations can change execution ordering.

nodes.label: Session event log
nodes.subtitle: Model-visible means logged

responsibility.text: Uses append-only session events as the source for model history. Streaming UI chunks and settled durable records are distinct.

nodes.inputs: Committed request, response and tool facts
nodes.extension: Persistence and projection services are extensible.
nodes.failureMode: Failed and cancelled attempts must settle coherently in the log.

nodes.label: Native plugins + bridges
nodes.subtitle: Hooks · MCP · skills

responsibility.text: Adds native capabilities and compatibility bridges. The Codex hook bridge supports a documented subset.

nodes.inputs: External bundles and existing hook configuration
nodes.extension: Live plugin activation, preset composition and typed events.
nodes.failureMode: An in-process plugin is not contained by the workspace tool sandbox.

nodes.label: Interaction + approval
nodes.subtitle: Pause for a decision

responsibility.text: Coordinates permission decisions and escalation around tool execution.

nodes.extension: Interaction and sandbox services form separate seams.
nodes.failureMode: An approval does not prove that every operation is isolated.

nodes.label: Sandbox backend
nodes.subtitle: Platform-specific execution

responsibility.text: Provides local Linux, macOS and Windows execution backends with configured access modes.

nodes.inputs: An execution request and access mode
nodes.outputs: Tool output under the selected restrictions
nodes.failureMode: The project warns that its preview controls do not guarantee isolation.

chapters.title: A composable core
chapters.heading: The loop is a plugin
chapters.body: Start with the Cordis context: services and typed events compose the runtime.
chapters.takeaway: The central loop is one replaceable capability in the tree.

chapters.title: A guarded pipeline
chapters.heading: Where plugins intervene
chapters.body: Trace a call through pre-execution, execution and post-execution events.
chapters.takeaway: An extension can intercept behavior without editing the caller.

chapters.title: Execution boundary
chapters.heading: Two trust boundaries
chapters.body: Tool sandboxing and host plugin execution have different authority.
chapters.takeaway: Installed host plugins execute outside the workspace tool sandbox.

chapters.title: The event log
chapters.heading: History is a projection
chapters.body: The durable log supplies model-visible context; transient UI streaming is a separate concern.
chapters.takeaway: Persist facts, then derive the context that a model sees.

chapters.title: Profiles and bridges
chapters.heading: Compose a different agent
chapters.body: Inspect bundle layering and compatibility with existing Codex hook files.
chapters.takeaway: Interoperability is observable evidence. It does not establish copying.
